Based on RAN3 LS R3-174964, RAN2 defined a new RRC inter-node message in TS38.331 for SMTC information, considering future extension (eg. CSI-RS), the message is named as “MeasurementTimingConfiguration”. After RAN2_101bis meeting, based on CR R2-1806431, the detail parameters are initially finalized. In RAN2 spec (i.e., TS38.331), the structure of the MeasurementTimingConfiguration message is per frequency level as shown in the following figure: Figure 1 Structure of MeasurementTimingConfiguration in 38.331 However in latest RAN3 spec TS 36.423 v15.1.0, the usage of MeasurementTimingConfiguration is illustrated in the following figure (e.g. take EN-DC X2 SETUP REQUEST message and EN-DC CONFIGURATION UPDATE message as examples), which is per cell level. Figure 2 Structure of MeasurementTimingConfiguration in 36.423 Then for cell specific X2 procedure, the whole structure becomes: Figure 3 Combined structure of MeasurementTimingConfiguration As shown in Figure 3, RAN2 defines the inter-node message to contain a list of frequencies, and corresponding SMTC configurations, but the inter-node message is used under per Cell configuration in RAN3. Observation 1: MeasurementTimingConfiguration is configured per frequency in TS38.331, but it is configured per cell in TS36.423, which is misaligned. Observation 2: According to RAN2 and RAN3 specification, for a given cell, MeasurementTimingConfiguration can include a list of frequencies and corresponding SMTC configurations. In order to avoid misleading in RAN3 specification, for per-cell level information transmission, we can add more detail semantics description for the Measurement Timing Configuration IE to instruct the network implementation. Proposal 1: Add semantics description for the Measurement Timing Configuration IE in TS 36.423 to clarify that only the frequency and SMTC configuration of the corresponding cell is included, rather than a list of frequencies and SMTC configurations. Proposal 2: Change the IE description of Measurement Timing Configuration in TS 36.423 from “IE” to “RRC message”.

t side is the proposal for the revised structure) Clarification for some of the intentions On section 10 of the current structure in v0.4.0 (“Ultra-Reliable and Low Latency Communications”): This section is proposed to be deleted as URLLC is a use case (and there is a dedicated section to capture URLLC requirements already in section 4.1). Functions, architecture, interfaces and procedures related to support of URLLC requirements, if required, should be captured in the respective sections (i.e. section 6, 7, 10 of the proposal for the revised structure). On section 6.1 of the proposal for the revised structure (“RAN-CN functional split”): High level text on RAN-CN functional split expected for this section (intention is to just to show the overview). It is expected to transpose contents from this section to RAN TR 38.912 section 10.1 (in a similar manner to the LTE TR 25.912 section 9.2). On section 6.2 of the proposal for the revised structure (“RAN functions description”): Section 6.2 is the function list. Contents of section 6.1.1.1 of the current structure in v0.4.0 (“Functions for New RAN”) will be moved here. Subsections (i.e. 6.2.x) can be introduced here for more descriptive (but limited) text when needed (e.g. for newer functions). For example, there is already a subsection under section 6.1.1.1 of the current structure in v0.4.0, i.e. 6.1.1.1.1 ("Support for a UE operational mode during periods of no traffic [FFS RAN2]"). Detailed call flows with sequence charts should not be captured in this section (instead, they should be captured in section 9). On section 7 of the proposal for the revised structure (“RAN Architecture and Interfaces”): The title of this section is made to be "RAN architecture" instead of "New RAN Architecture" since architectures with EPC connectivity should also be captured here (as is already the case in section 6.3.1 of the current structure in v0.4.0). On section 10 of the proposal for the revised structure (“Radio access network procedures”): Section 10 is for detailed call flows and sequence charts for key procedures (e.g. dual connectivity, mobility, network slicing, etc.). It is expected to transpose some or all of the procedures illustrated here to RAN TR 38.912 section 12 (in a similar manner to the LTE TR 25.912 sections 9.4 to 9.7). On section 10.1 of the proposal for the revised structure (“Tight interworking between New RAT and LTE”): Section 10.1 if for Dual/Multi Connectivity procedures. It is expected to transpose contents from this section to RAN TR 38.912 section 12.1. On section 10.2.1 of the proposal for the revised structure (“Mobility without CN type change”: Section 10.2.1 can include all mobility procedures for New RAN operation, except those with CN type change. I.e. all mobility (without EPC<=>NGC change). E.g. idle/in-active/connected mobility intra-RAT/System mobility with/without CN change mobility between eLTE and gNB … On section 10.2.2 of the proposal for the revised structure (“Mobility with CN type change”): Section 10.2.2 is dedicated to mobility procedures for New RAN operation with CN type change (i.e. EPC<=>NGC change). On section 10.2.3 of the proposal for the revised structure (“XXX”): This is just for illustration that new sub-sections can be introduced based on future TP input for New RAN procedures other than mobility. (And so this section will not appear in the TR update to v0.5.0). On section 15 of the proposal for the revised structure (“Interworking with non-3GPP systems”): Architecture, interfaces and procedures for non-3GPP interworking will all be captured here (i.e. it will not be distributed to over sections 6, 7 and 10). Proposal: Agree to revise the TR 38.801 structure as illustrated in Figure 1. R3-162468, “Proposal for TR 38.801 structure change”, TR

Based on the discussion in [1] and [2], this contribution proposes text proposal for TS 38.423 on QoS parameters including: - Add UE Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate IE in section 9.1.1.1 HANDOVER REQUEST message; - Add Reflective QoS Attribute IE in section 9.2.1 QoS Flow Level Parameters; - Add Default Allocation and Retention Priority IE in section 9.2.100 PDU Session Resource Setup List and section 9.2.101 PDU Session Resource Modify List; - Introduce Averaging Window (FFS) IE in section 9.2.2 QoS Flow Level Parameters; - Define Allocation and Retention Priority IE in section 9.2.X (new); - Define Non-standardised QoS Flow Descriptor IE in section 9.2.Y (new); - Move Notification Control IE in section 9.2.1 QoS Flow Level Parameters to section 9.2.2 QoS Flow Level Parameters; since the IE is used for GBR bearer; - Remove FFS on 5QI in section 9.2.2 QoS Flow Level Parameters. START OF CHANGE This message is sent by the source NG-RAN node to the target NG-RAN node to request the preparation of resources for a handover. Direction: source NG-RAN node  target NG-RAN node. This IE defines the QoS to be applied to a QoS flow. This IE indicates the maximum and guaranteed bit rates of a GBR QoS flows for downlink and uplink. Editor’s Note: Most probably this IE will be incorporated directly into the message structure and not defined as a separate IE. In principle it is applicable for Xn-C messages for HO/DC/RRC INACTIVE mobility (UE Context Retrieval) (as a PDU Session Resource configuration descriptor). Editor’s Note: Most probably this IE will be incorporated directly into the message structure and not defined as a separate IE. In principle it is applicable for Xn-C messages for DC (if configuration modification information needs to be relayed to the SN). . END OF CHANGE
